{{Short description|American evolutionary biologist (born 1951)}}

'''John Norton Thompson''' (born November 15, 1951) is an American [[evolutionary biologist]]. He is [[Jean H. Langeheim]] Professor of Plant Ecology and Evolution at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]].<ref name="CV" />

Thompson is known for his research on [[coevolution]]. He proposed the [[Coevolution#Geographic_mosaic_theory|geographic mosaic theory of coevolution]].<ref name="ucsc">{{Cite web|last=Stephens|first=Tim|title=Evolutionary biologist John Thompson awarded Darwin-Wallace Medal|url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2017/05/thompson-medal.html|work=UC Santa Cruz News|date=26 May 2017 |accessdate=2021-10-06}}</ref>

== Background ==
Thompson was born in [[Pittsburgh]] on November 15, 1951. In 1973 he graduated from [[Washington & Jefferson College|Washington & Jefferson]] College in Washington, Pennsylvania with a bachelor's degree and in 1977 received his PhD in ecology from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]].<ref name="CV">{{Cite web| title = Contact & CV {{!}} The John N Thompson Lab| accessdate = 2021-10-06| url = https://thompsonlab.sites.ucsc.edu/contact/}}</ref> His dissertation was entitled "Patch Dynamics in the Insect - ''Pastinaca sativa'' Association: Life History Tactics and Population Consequences." 

Afterwards he became Visiting Assistant Professor for Entomology. 

In 1978 he became Assistant Professor; 1982 Associate Professor; and 1987 Professor at [[Washington State University]], where from 1994 he was Edward Meyer Distinguished Professor. 

In 1991-2 he was a [[Fulbright]] Scholar in Canberra, Australia. 

In 2000 he became Professor of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]], where he was Director of the STEPS Institute for Innovation in Environmental Research from 2002 to 2007. 

In 2008 he became a Distinguished Professor; and in 2014 was appointed the Jean H. Langeheim Professor of Plant Ecology and Evolution.<ref name="CV"></ref>

In 2014 he was a visiting fellow at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].<ref name="CV"></ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
In 2008 he was President of the [[American Society of Naturalists]].<ref name="ucsc" />

In 2017 he received the [[Darwin-Wallace Medal]] for his work on coevolution.<ref name="ucsc"></ref>

He is a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[California Academy of Sciences]], and the [[Royal Entomological Society of London]].<ref>{{Cite web| title = John N. Thompson| work = American Academy of Arts & Sciences| accessdate = 2021-10-06| url = https://www.amacad.org/person/john-n-thompson}}</ref>

He is one of the ISI Highly Cited Researchers in Evolutionary Biology and Ecology.<ref name="CV"></ref>
